learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 60%, the simple average of 80% and 40%, and locked it in for budgets 300 and 100 dollars.
observations.exploration: Initial pool put 280 of 400 dollars on A, implied 70%. Equal money preset changed both budgets to 200 and implied 60%. Bettor 2 richer reversed budgets to 100/300 and implied 50%. Start restored 70%, retained comparison summaries and unlocked reveal.
observations.reveal: Corrected 70%. Explains 240 plus 40 dollars on A out of 400, then connects equal and reversed budgets to wealth-weighted average belief. Model assumes no house cut and all money split according to belief.
observations.visual: Inspected inline reversed-budget screenshot: pool segments labelled by bettor and dollars, solid odds line at 50% versus dashed simple-average line at 60%. Controls and retained summaries legible. Trust count 4/4 ignored.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: Clear unequal-budget setup tests unweighted averaging.

interaction.reason: Equal, reversed and restored budgets isolate weighting while beliefs and total money stay fixed.

payoff.reason: Connects all tested states to explicit contributions and weighted-average rule under model conditions.
payoff.evidence: 240+40 out of 400, equal and reversed comparisons.

clarity.reason: Segment labels and solid-versus-dashed reference make the distinction readable.

transfer.reason: Reusable weighting principle and model conditions given without concrete new market case.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Simple-average prediction fails when money weights differ.

visualExplanation.reason: Pool segments and moving line relative to fixed average carry mechanism across controlled contrasts.

playfulness.reason: Presets, slider and restore allow reversible weight experiments.

practicalValue.reason: Concrete interpretation of pooled betting odds, with restrictive assumptions.
practicalValue.evidence: No house cut and belief-proportional spending.

depth.reason: Individual beliefs, capital weights and fixed arithmetic mean are separated.

complexity.reason: Combines weighted contributions and total share while keeping beliefs fixed.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: moderate: implied chance and money weighting
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: moderate: budgets, percentages and pool fraction

whyCool: Reversing who has more money moves the odds from 70% to 50% while both beliefs and their simple average stay unchanged.
caveat: The toy spending rule does not test strategic betting, prices, or actual probability accuracy.
